aspect: effective dating, versioning and historical reconstruction
gap: Library rates carry effective dating and row history, estimates carry versions with pinned library snapshots, and plans now carry versions. No financial record does: a pay application, a job cost and a payable each have one current state and no history beyond the audit ledger, so a prior period cannot be reconstructed as it stood.

There is no ledger to balance to. Individual arithmetic is defended — a pay application cannot bill more than the contract sum plus approved changes, a work order's total is generated from its parts, an achieved production rate is a generated column — but no double entry exists and nothing can be unbalanced.

Statuses are explicit and constrained, and transitions are enforced — a pay application cannot leave draft without a submission timestamp, a claim cannot advance past potential without a notice date, an executed change order cannot move back. None of it is configurable: the states and the transitions are in the schema, and a company cannot add a review step of its own.

Dashboards and drill-downs exist as screens over five reporting views, each with security_invoker so a view can never become the way around row level security.
